failure_policy: Any failing required job MUST fail the pipeline.
A pipeline MUST NOT turn blocking failures into warnings for protected branches.
Automatic rerun-until-green behavior MUST NOT be treated as release proof for a failing blocking job.
Skipped or absent required jobs are failures, not neutral states.
Protected-branch proof MUST come from required jobs running against the pinned toolchain, not from a contributor-local variant.
A quarantined test is debt, not a pass; protected-branch CI MUST surface quarantine state explicitly.

contracts_runtime_suite.purpose: Executes the runtime harness proof surface required by TG-0 dynamic assertions.

contracts_strict.purpose: Prevents contract drift, bundle mismatch, and gate linkage failures.

governance_lint.purpose: Prevents banned governance patterns and waiver abuse from entering the repository.

integration_suite.purpose: Proves database-backed flows and denial-path correctness remain intact.

property_suite.purpose: Exercises generated invariants that catch drift beyond fixed examples.

quality_static.design_note: This job intentionally overlaps with targeted suite jobs so the normative developer entrypoint and the CI entrypoints cannot drift apart silently.
quality_static.purpose: Runs formatting, compile, Credo, Dialyzer, and the full deterministic ExUnit surface through the mandated entrypoint.

unit_suite.design_note: Fast isolation lane for pure logic drift.
unit_suite.purpose: Provides fast isolation for deterministic pure logic regressions.

required_evidence: Blocking mix test jobs MUST emit the ExUnit seed in CI logs.
Property test failures MUST emit enough seed and counterexample information to reproduce the failure locally.
Protected-branch CI logs MUST retain the full failing command and failing suite path.

constitutional_mapping.why: Ledger and payout errors are not acceptable and require both example-based and generative proof.
Inventory drift and oversell behavior require denial-path and generated-case coverage.
Cross-tenant leakage is a hard failure and must be tested directly.
User-safe errors and emitted signals must stay aligned.
Dynamic gates are false comfort unless they execute through a repository harness.

rules: Line-coverage thresholds MAY be collected, but they MUST NOT be the sole merge or release proof for correctness.
A high aggregate coverage percentage MUST NOT waive missing denial-path, tenancy, ledger, inventory, or regression suites.
Coverage reports are evidence supplements, not substitutes, for the blocking QA-0 suite topology.

applies_to: test/regression when persistence or concurrency is exercised
rules: Database-backed tests MUST use an isolation mechanism such as SQL sandbox or an equivalent per-test transaction boundary.
Tests that mutate shared persisted state MUST clean up deterministically; order-dependent leakage between tests is forbidden.
Async database-backed tests are allowed only when the isolation mechanism and shared fixtures prove they cannot interfere.

Defines strict CI validation expectations for contract bundles and canonical pinning behavior.
Defines Ash 3.x governance rules that QA-0 requires the implementation repository to enforce continuously.
Provides deterministic governance scanning rules that QA-0 treats as a required blocking CI job.
Provides tenancy invariants that QA-0 requires dedicated denial-path test suites to preserve.
Provides canonical error envelope expectations that QA-0 requires tests to assert.
Provides the constitutional invariants that QA-0 maps to executable repo checks.

determinism_policy.clock: Tests that depend on time MUST freeze, inject, or deterministically control time rather than reading ambient wall-clock state.
determinism_policy.external_dependencies: Unit and integration suites MUST stub or fake unstable external dependencies; live external calls belong only in separately-governed suites outside the default blocking ExUnit surface.
determinism_policy.parallelism: Suites MAY run asynchronously only when shared-state isolation is proven; hidden test-order coupling is forbidden.
determinism_policy.randomness: Property and randomized tests MUST capture failing seeds and bound execution so failures are reproducible.
determinism_policy.seed_reporting: CI and local reruns MUST preserve and expose failing ExUnit and property-test seeds so counterexamples are replayable.

forbidden_shortcuts: mix test --only <subset> used as merge proof for protected branches
mix test --exclude <blocking_tag> used as merge proof for protected branches
Environment-variable branches that silently downgrade required suites
global_rules: CI MUST print the ExUnit seed for every blocking mix test invocation so failures are reproducible.
The default blocking ExUnit surface MUST be deterministic, non-interactive, and runnable from a clean checkout without manual environment mutation.
A repository MUST NOT rely on test order, previously persisted database state, or leftover files from earlier runs.

foundation_refs.reason: V42 is the constitutional foundation; QA-0 defines executable QA and regression-prevention discipline without weakening those invariants.

supersedes.reason: Hardens the QA standard while preserving contract intent.

prohibitions: A repository MUST NOT redefine mix check as a non-blocking convenience command.
A repository MUST NOT exclude regression, tenancy, security, property, or contracts_runtime suites from mix test for speed unless QA-0 is revised.
A repository MUST NOT treat compiler warnings as informational only.
A repository MUST NOT claim protected-branch proof from mix test invocations that use only or exclude flags to bypass required suites.
A repository MUST NOT move required blocking suites outside test/ and still describe the default surface as QA-0 compliant.

mix_check.rule: The command order is normative. A repository MUST NOT silently weaken mix check by removing, reordering, or downgrading these steps without a QA-0 version bump.

mix_test.rule: mix test MUST execute the full deterministic blocking ExUnit surface under test/ including regression, tenancy, security, property, and contracts_runtime suites.

mix_test_integration.rule: The repository MUST provide a stable way to run integration and denial-path suites together.

mix_test_property.rule: The repository MUST provide a stable way to run property tests alone with deterministic seed capture.

mix_test_regression.rule: The repository MUST provide a stable way to run permanent regression tests alone.

mix_test_runtime.rule: The repository MUST provide a stable way to run runtime-harness-backed contract tests alone.

mix_test_unit.rule: The repository MUST provide a stable way to run the unit suite alone.

new_proposed_invariants.statement: The implementation repository MUST define a stable mix check entrypoint with a fixed ordered command chain so repo-wide quality enforcement does not drift by contributor, branch, or agent.
new_proposed_invariants.title: mix check is mandatory and ordered

new_proposed_invariants.statement: Blocking tests MUST live in deterministic path classes under test/ so mix test and CI jobs can select suites without tag ambiguity.
new_proposed_invariants.title: Directory-first ExUnit classification is mandatory

new_proposed_invariants.statement: Any bugfix, incident patch, or hotfix MUST add or update a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after the fix.
new_proposed_invariants.title: Every defect fix requires a permanent reproducer test

new_proposed_invariants.statement: If any contract gate declares a TG-0 dynamic runtime assertion primitive, the repository MUST provide test/support/v42_harness.ex and a blocking runtime harness CI job.
new_proposed_invariants.title: Harness interlock is repo law

new_proposed_invariants.statement: A failing blocking test suite MUST fail the pipeline; automatic rerun-until-green behavior MUST NOT be used as release proof.
new_proposed_invariants.title: Flaky green-through-rerun is banned

new_proposed_invariants.statement: Property-based tests MUST run with deterministic seed capture and bounded execution settings so failures can be reproduced exactly.
new_proposed_invariants.title: Property tests must be reproducible

new_proposed_invariants.statement: Protected-branch CI MUST execute on explicitly pinned Elixir and OTP versions so test outcomes do not drift across machines.
new_proposed_invariants.title: Pinned toolchains are mandatory for protected-branch proof

new_proposed_invariants.statement: Global ExUnit configuration MUST originate from test/test_helper.exs so seed handling, exclusions, and support wiring remain auditable.
new_proposed_invariants.title: test/test_helper.exs owns global ExUnit setup

new_proposed_invariants.statement: Focused tests, committed skip tags, and silent quarantine patterns MUST NOT be used as protected-branch merge proof.
new_proposed_invariants.title: Focus, skip, and quarantine abuse are banned

new_proposed_invariants.statement: Database-backed suites MUST use deterministic isolation such as SQL sandbox or equivalent per-test transaction boundaries.
new_proposed_invariants.title: Database-backed tests require deterministic isolation

new_proposed_invariants.statement: Coverage thresholds MUST NOT replace invariant-mapped negative tests, tenancy tests, or regression suites.
new_proposed_invariants.title: Coverage is evidence, not proof

new_proposed_invariants.statement: High-risk contract implementations MUST preserve a discoverable path from governing doc_id or invariant family to blocking test modules.
new_proposed_invariants.title: High-risk contracts must remain traceable to tests

non_goals: QA-0 does not redefine business semantics already owned by subsystem contracts.
QA-0 does not define performance-load tooling owned by PSC-1 or incident operations owned by OBS-1.
QA-0 does not relax V42, tenancy, pricing, ledger, or seat invariants for implementation convenience.
purpose.one_liner: Locks the repository execution, ExUnit, and CI quality regime required to prevent implementation regressions and governance drift after development begins.
scope: mix entrypoints that MUST exist and remain stable.
ExUnit suite topology and blocking categories.
CI jobs that MUST block merge and release.
Runtime harness obligations for TG-0 dynamic assertions.
Regression-test obligations for defects, incidents, and hotfixes.
Toolchain, lockfile, formatter, and test-helper ownership needed for reproducible QA execution.
Quarantine, focus, skip, and database-isolation discipline for blocking suites.
Coverage and traceability rules that prevent false confidence and unowned regressions.
why: Contracts without executable repo checks still allow code-level drift.
A deterministic test topology is required so coding agents and humans produce the same enforcement surface.
Bug fixes without permanent reproducer tests cause repeat incidents.
Unpinned toolchains and ad hoc ExUnit globals create machine-specific false greens and false reds.
Skip/focus abuse and weak quarantine discipline silently hollow out protected-branch confidence.
Coverage percentages without invariant-mapped tests create measurement theater, not safety.

rules: Focused tests, committed skip tags, and blanket skip exclusions MUST NOT be used on protected branches as a substitute for fixing the suite.
Any temporary quarantine of a blocking test MUST be recorded in a machine-readable registry with an issue reference, owner, expiry date, and containment note.
A quarantined test MUST remain visible in CI output as quarantined debt; silent disappearance is forbidden.
quarantine_control_policy.why: The fastest way to rot a suite is to hide failing tests behind convenience tags and call the branch green.

regression_prevention_policy.bugfix_rule: Every defect fix, incident remediation, and hotfix MUST include a reproducer test added or updated under the appropriate blocking suite before merge.
regression_prevention_policy.incident_rule: If a production incident escaped existing tests, the post-incident patch MUST add at least one permanent regression test that would have prevented the escape.
regression_prevention_policy.naming_rule: Regression tests SHOULD encode the invariant or defect class in the test module or test name so the preserved lesson remains discoverable.
regression_prevention_policy.quarantine_registry_rule: If a regression test is temporarily quarantined, the quarantine registry entry MUST reference the exact regression test, incident or defect identifier, owner, expiry, and compensating control.
regression_prevention_policy.waiver_rule: Temporary skipping or quarantine of a blocking regression test MUST carry an explicit issue reference, an owner, an expiry date, and a replacement containment measure; indefinite suppression is forbidden.

rules: Blocking deterministic suites MUST live under the declared test/ subpaths.
Load, soak, chaos, and benchmark suites MUST NOT hide under the default blocking ExUnit tree; they MUST live under a non-default path such as perf/ or bench/ and be governed separately.
A repository MAY add more test/ subpaths, but it MUST NOT repurpose the required path classes for unrelated concerns.
Shared ExUnit helpers, case templates, and harness adapters MUST live under test/support unless a downstream contract explicitly governs another location.
Production lib/ modules MUST NOT become the hiding place for test-only helper behavior that changes blocking suite semantics.

runtime_harness_contract.ci_rule: CI MUST run a dedicated blocking job for runtime harness tests whenever any contracts_runtime tests exist or any dynamic runtime gates are present in the suite.
must_provide: A deterministic adapter callable from ExUnit tests.
Fixture loading for Ash actions, HTTP routes, and worker jobs as required by TG-0 trigger schemas.
Capture helpers for telemetry, tracing, and canonical error envelope assertions.
Stable helper functions that allow contract-runtime tests to assert doc_id- and invariant-specific outcomes without copy-pasted ad hoc harness code.
runtime_harness_contract.trigger_rule: This file becomes mandatory when any suite contract declares TG-0 dynamic runtime assertion primitives.

summary: Enterprise QA execution standard for Ash 3.x Elixir repositories: locks mix entrypoints, ExUnit suite topology, CI release blockers, runtime harness requirements, and defect-to-regression-test workflow.

rules: test/test_helper.exs MUST be the single root for global ExUnit configuration.
Global test exclusions, case templates, sandbox checkout helpers, and seed/reporting configuration MUST be wired from test/test_helper.exs or files it explicitly requires under test/support.
test/test_helper.exs MUST NOT silently exclude any blocking QA-0 suite or tag class on protected branches.

must_prove: TG-0 dynamic runtime assertions are executable in-repo using the harness adapter.
Telemetry, spans, and error-envelope-to-signal correlations required by contract gates are testable and blocking.
Ash domains, resources, actions, repo persistence, and transaction boundaries preserve contract semantics end to end.
Database-backed flows preserve invariants under normal success and expected business-failure paths.
Invariant-heavy logic such as ledger balancing, idempotency normalization, UUID ordering rules, allocation monotonicity, or snapshot immutability holds across generated cases.
Seeds, bounds, and shrinking output are captured so failures are reproducible.
Every previously fixed defect, incident class, or contract drift case remains permanently covered by a concrete reproducer test.
Regression tests MUST be named after the invariant, defect class, or incident they prevent.
Authorization denials, enumeration resistance, idempotency abuse prevention, replay resistance, and privileged boundary checks remain intact.
Public error responses remain user-safe and do not leak tenant existence or internal state.
Cross-tenant reads, writes, relationship traversals, background jobs, and administrative boundaries fail closed.
Canonical tenant key usage remains org_id only.
Pure domain logic, validation modules, policy helpers, serializers, calculators, and canonical formatters behave deterministically.
No network I/O, filesystem I/O, or cross-process orchestration is required.

test_taxonomy.negative_test_rule: High-risk invariants for tenancy, authorization, money, ledger, inventory, scanning, and idempotency MUST include explicit denial-path tests, not only happy-path assertions.
test_taxonomy.selection_rule: mix test MUST execute all deterministic blocking categories under test/ by default.

title: QA Execution, ExUnit, and Regression Prevention Standard

rules: Protected-branch CI MUST run on explicitly pinned Elixir and OTP versions recorded in .tool-versions or an equivalently committed repository file.
The repository MUST commit mix.lock and MUST treat dependency graph drift as a reviewed change, not an ambient CI variable.
The repository MUST provide .formatter.exs and MUST keep formatting deterministic across developer and CI environments.
toolchain_contract.why: Unpinned toolchains and floating dependency graphs create false regressions, false greens, and non-reproducible ExUnit behavior.

rules: High-risk subsystem implementations MUST have at least one blocking test module whose name, tag, or module documentation references the governing doc_id or invariant family.
When a contract invariant fails in production, the replacement regression test MUST be traceable back to the governing doc_id, incident, or defect class.
